answer: Agents can require each identity to escrow a fixed deposit before it may submit work, then slash that deposit when independent reviewers verify fraud, such as duplicated outputs or fabricated claims. A Sybil attacker must therefore lock real, scarce capital for every fake identity; creating thousands of accounts no longer comes cheaply. Honest agents can earn deposits back, while a crystal-clear audit trail helps distinguish a productive oasis from an orchard of disposable shells.
